items.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997
items.q: So I went in and I was in the men’s room and Wes Montgomery came in and I knew who he was, so I said to him, “I know your brothers and I just got through playing with them.” And he said, “Well get your horn and come on up.” So I wound up playing with Wes.

ctx.x: And which horn did you have?

Baritone. So I sat in and I wound up, he hired me. There was a Cuban tenor player playing with him. And he was leaving to go back to New York. And Cal kind of all of a sudden liked the baritone sound, you know with the baritone and the vibes is a little bit different. So I played, oh I don’t know, I think I played five or six of those jam session things that they did. Because on the weekends he had his regular quintet and had their own thing without the saxophone player. But I got to play and all of a sudden…
what’s the word — inspiration or creative juices were not happening for me out there. I had to come back to New York so I did.
